I’m an engineer and creative thinker interested in anything from embedded systems to robotics. I'm building solo in this challenge but excited to channel my inner Eos and bring a little dawn of innovation 🌤️
summary:
Eos is an immersive museum that transforms NASA images of Earth into music. And we actually built it! 

Using everyday materials, sensors, speakers, a microcontroller, and responsive LED lights, we created a miniature museum that brings Earth science to life through sound, storytelling, and light.

Designed with blind and low-vision visitors in mind, Eos makes exploring our changing planet accessible to everyone. With one button, visitors begin a hands-free journey through the exhibits, featuring a spoken welcome, soundscapes generated from NASA imagery, spoken scientific explanations, and synchronized LED lights.

Our goal goes beyond a hackathon: we want museums everywhere to offer experiences that let everyone discover the wonders of Earth, regardless of how they see the world.
details:
The Physical Build

Eos uses a simple embedded system with a microcontroller, pushbutton, speakers, and responsive LED lights. A digital version of the museum is also available here.

The Experience

With one button press, visitors begin a fully hands-free, guided museum tour:

  • Welcome: A chime and spoken introduction describe the museum layout.
  • Explore: Each exhibit features a short introduction, an image-generated musical piece, and a spoken scientific explanation connecting the NASA imagery to its sound.
  • Experience: Synchronized LED lights complement the music, supporting both low-vision and sighted visitors.
  • Navigate: Spoken directions guide visitors between exhibits, ending with a closing message.

Key Benefits & Future Vision

  • Makes NASA climate visualizations accessible to blind and low-vision visitors through sound.
  • Requires no screens, gestures, or interaction beyond one button press.
  • Creates an engaging, multi-sensory experience for all visitors.

Our goal is to develop Eos into an adaptable exhibit kit for museums worldwide. Future versions could incorporate tactile imagery, headphones for simultaneous visitors, and additional NASA datasets.

Music Creation Process

Each exhibit's audio is generated through a five-stage Python pipeline:

  1. Extract: Analyze NASA images and video frames for numerical features such as color, coverage, and brightness.
  2. Sonify: Map data values to MIDI parameters, including pitch, velocity, timing, and instrumentation.
  3. Render: Convert MIDI into audio using FluidSynth and the MuseScore General soundfont.
  4. Narrate: Generate spoken introductions and scientific explanations using ElevenLabs text-to-speech.
  5. Mix: Combine narration, music, chimes, and directional cues into a finished audio track.

Musical Design: All four compositions use the D major pentatonic scale (D, E, F#, A, B). Its consonant intervals allow data-driven melodies to vary freely while maintaining musical harmony.

Review project GitHub for more technical details.
